Topics.Title: Start here: read a finding or trace a path
Topics.Summary: Use Saved findings to review a recorded exposure candidate, Objects & relationships to inspect evidence, and Paths & graph to ask a directed reachability question.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Open the intended completed report. Inspect the source, target, relationship direction and collection window before considering a change.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: The viewer reads a saved snapshot; it does not query AD or apply a recommendation. A candidate is a review lead, not confirmed compromise.

Topics.Title: Source, target and path direction
Topics.Summary: An arrow runs from the principal with a modeled capability to the object it can affect. Find path returns the union of all equally short directed routes.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Enter an exact name or identifier. DA resolves Domain Admins only when unambiguous. If a name matches several objects, choose its exact ID. Swap ends reverses the question and the waypoint order.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A table in all-shortest mode is an edge set, not one sequential path. Longer detours are omitted. A domain-control capability may target the domain itself rather than the Domain Admins group.

Topics.Terms: DA Domain Admins target corp source target arrows reverse

Topics.Title: Via 1 and Via 2
Topics.Summary: Waypoints require the route to visit specified objects in order: Source → Via 1 → Via 2 → Target. Blank waypoints are skipped.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Use waypoints to test a proposed intermediate group or host. Read each leg's result when a leg fails or reaches a work limit.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Each leg retains its shortest alternatives; the combined graph may revisit objects. This does not enumerate all possible simple paths.

Topics.Title: Routes to target: shortest or all connections
Topics.Summary: Routes searches backwards from the target independently of the source and waypoint boxes.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Choose Target: shortest for edges on shortest routes to the target. Choose all connections to include supported reverse-reachable detours and cycles.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: All connections is not a count of attack scenarios or infinitely repeated cyclic walks. Dense administrator relationships can be expected context.

Topics.Title: Relationship filters
Topics.Summary: The checked relationship types determine which capabilities a path query can use.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Start with all types, then narrow the question. Clear-all intentionally permits no relationship types. Check filters when an expected path disappears.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A label being available in a filter does not mean that it was collected, derived or traversable in this snapshot. Inventory facts are not automatically control edges.

Topics.Title: Visit, time and display limits
Topics.Summary: Queries have independent work and display budgets. A visit is an identity examined, not a count of complete routes.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Read the result status and any failed waypoint leg. Increase the visit budget or narrow the source/target if work stops early. Cancel stops the active local query.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: VisitLimit, SearchEdgeLimit, timeout, cancellation and a displayed edge limit are incomplete results, not evidence of no path. A bounded preview can be smaller than the stored graph.

Topics.Title: Read a dense graph
Topics.Summary: Select a connection to list its individual relationship types; numbered curves identify parallel permissions. Select a row for the matching explanation.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Drag to pan, use the mouse wheel or +/- to zoom, Fit to see the graph bounds, and Read for readable node labels. Previous/Next select nodes; Inspect opens their properties.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A bundled connection can represent several relationships. Arrow direction matters. Expanding one connection does not discover additional directory facts.

Topics.Title: Saved findings and priority
Topics.Summary: Saved findings retain representative shortest recorded chains from identities to the selected targets. Priority is a review-ranking heuristic.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Open the path, inspect each capability and its evidence, and validate the actual permissions and service prerequisites. Use on-demand path search for equally short alternatives.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: One saved candidate is not every possible route. Membership-only context is not a new escalation finding. High priority is not an exploitation verdict or a CVSS score.

Topics.Terms: score high medium priority risk severity

Topics.Title: Pages, filters and report previews
Topics.Summary: The native viewer pages over saved candidates and collected objects; the HTML report includes bounded previews.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Use the page controls and search the full native index when a name is absent from the HTML preview. Reset search fields if the result count seems unexpected.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Page size, embedded preview size, search-work limits and total saved counts are different quantities. Empty filtered results do not establish an empty dataset.

Topics.Title: Object search and navigation
Topics.Summary: Search matches names and identifiers in the selected index. Inspect shows the retained record and paged incoming or outgoing relationships.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Check the SID/GUID rather than relying only on a display name. Use Back/Forward to revisit inspected objects and Source/Target to populate a path query.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A referenced identity may lack a collected object record. Missing properties may mean older data, unsupported collection or unreadable attributes; they are not automatically false.

Topics.Title: Incoming versus outgoing relationships
Topics.Summary: Incoming relationships describe what can affect the inspected object; outgoing relationships describe what that object can affect.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Choose the direction and relationship filter, then select a row to inspect its evidence. Inspect other object follows the opposite endpoint.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A relationship list includes inventory as well as capabilities. Graph relationship can display an inventory observation without making it part of control-path traversal.

Topics.Title: Continue a long recorded path
Topics.Summary: Long paths are displayed in segments so the interface stays usable. Continue loads the next segment from the indicated object.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Read the shown step range and remaining hop count. Retain every segment if documenting the complete chain.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A displayed or exported segment is not the whole path. Continued on-demand queries search from the continuation point using the selected supported relationships.

Topics.Title: Export a review plan
Topics.Summary: Export plan writes a local text explanation of the displayed relationships, their evidence, proposed remediation and validation steps.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Verify source/target IDs, waypoint order, segment limits and coverage before sharing it. Tailor proposed changes to the real service owner.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Exporting does not validate a route or perform any AD change. The plan may describe a segment or route edge set rather than one linear chain.

Topics.Title: Open latest and saved path rules
Topics.Summary: Open latest selects a completed report with a matching graph.sqlite. New application code and an old saved analysis can legitimately use different path-rule versions.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Reopen the updated scanner/viewer together. Regenerate the report from retained data when the saved rules differ. Confirm the full index path at the top of the viewer.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Regenerating cannot add missing collection evidence. A new scan is needed for newly collected fields; it is not required merely to recalculate supported paths.

Topics.Terms: outdated latest graph.sqlite stale version package

Topics.Title: Read-only collection and DC selection
Topics.Summary: Collection records directory objects, ACL observations and supported configuration using the selected identity. The DC picker uses available logon-DC information and cached domain-controller suggestions.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Confirm the domain, selected DC, search scope, included OUs and worker status. An unavailable suggested DC should not be treated as a verified connection; use Connect to test access.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Running the launcher as an administrator does not demonstrate ordinary-user coverage. Endpoint/service checks may have separate permission requirements; a skipped or denied check leaves a gap.

Topics.Terms: logon DC cache domain controller LDAP connection permissions OU read only scanner

Topics.Title: Scope, missing data and no path
Topics.Summary: Coverage describes what the scanner could observe, resolve and model in the supplied collection window.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Check scan/merge metadata, worker failures, endpoint status, unreadable security descriptors, unresolved IDs, supported relationship kinds and current filters.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: No path found means no route was found in the supported collected graph under this query's limits. It is not evidence that all attack paths are absent.

Topics.Terms: missing hidden broken no path coverage failed worker unresolved

Topics.Title: Merging scans and importing SharpHound
Topics.Summary: Merge deduplicates supported inventory and relationships; import maps supported SharpHound schema 5/6 records into Tessera's format.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Use original consistent snapshots and comparable collection times. Review skipped object types, source collection status and conflict notes after import or merge.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A merge does not make old facts simultaneous or improve permissions. Conflicting GPO, ownership or AD CS prerequisite snapshots suppress affected inferences. Azure/OpenGraph and many BloodHound derivations remain unsupported.

Topics.Terms: zip JSON schemas import merge duplicate conflict snapshot EnrichGroupTypes MaxGroupLookups EnrichmentSeconds read only LDAP group enrichment

Topics.Title: Quick, Deep, checkpoints and cancellation
Topics.Summary: Quick analysis uses configured depth/work budgets. Deep analysis can continue disk-backed discovery and save a checkpoint for a later resume.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Review mode, selected targets, depth/visit/time limits, completion status and checkpoint location. Resume with the same inputs and compatible path rules.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Completed means the supported selected search frontier was exhausted. It does not mean full BloodHound parity or complete collection. A canceled/time-limited analysis can retain partial results.

Topics.Terms: quick deep checkpoint resume frontier cancel completed incomplete

Topics.Title: New, still observed and no longer observed
Topics.Summary: Snapshot comparison describes whether a modeled chain was observed in the supplied current and baseline data.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Check both collection windows, permissions, source scopes and rule versions before attributing a difference to a security change.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: No longer observed can result from collection gaps or different inputs. It does not prove remediation. A newly observed path may have existed before the earlier collection.

Topics.Terms: baseline delta comparison newly observed still observed no longer observed

Topics.Title: Supported, conditional, candidate and suppressed
Topics.Summary: These labels describe a model's evidence state. Supported/candidate means collected prerequisites match a supported rule; conditional means material context remains uncertain.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Read the derivation-specific reason and witnesses. Suppressed relationships remain useful observations but are excluded from the affected automatic control projection.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Supported never means full-token effective access or successful exploitation was tested. Raw/limited ownership observations and unsupported configurations must not be read as confirmed control.

Topics.Terms: verified supported conditional suppressed candidate confidence

Topics.Title: Use remediation guidance safely
Topics.Summary: Recommendations identify which delegation, membership, configuration or administration practice to review; Tessera applies none of them.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Confirm the business owner, preserve the original setting, narrow the actual unnecessary prerequisite, then rescan alternatives and test legitimate workflows. Use the saved original setting for a scoped rollback if needed.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Do not remove a shared administrator group or reset credentials solely because it appears on a path. Expected administration, service dependencies and inheritance can explain many recorded relationships.

Topics.Terms: fix remediation recommendation rollback validation opsec operational impact

Topics.Title: Users and service identities
Topics.Summary: A directory user can represent a person, service or managed service account.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Review account state, security groups, delegated rights and observed sessions. Distinguish a gMSA/MSA from a conventional user by captured object classes and ownership context.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A user object is not evidence of an active session, a known password or current authentication ability.

Topics.Title: Security and distribution groups
Topics.Summary: Groups organize principals; security-enabled groups can contribute authorization SIDs to a token.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Check SecurityEnabled, nested memberships, membership-management rights and any downstream privileged access.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A name such as Admins does not establish privilege. Unknown/distribution group state is insufficient for the derived membership rules that require a security token.

Topics.Title: Computer accounts and endpoint observations
Topics.Summary: A computer account is a directory identity for a device; endpoint access is separate evidence.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Review Disabled/AccountStateKnown, SPNs, delegation, key credentials, local access observations and collection time.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Directory control is not the same as verified local administrator execution. Endpoint authorization and availability still matter.

Topics.Title: Domains and domain-root permissions
Topics.Summary: A domain is an AD security and naming boundary. Some capabilities such as DCSync and supported ESC1 candidates target the domain itself.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Review domain-root ACLs, replication witnesses, trust inventory and captured policy context.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A path ending at the domain need not pass through the Domain Admins group. Unmodeled trust relationships do not connect domains automatically.

Topics.Title: OUs and directory containers
Topics.Summary: Containers organize objects and may hold delegated ACLs or policy links.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Confirm the actual object class and distinguished-name containment. Review inherited ACLs and supported GPO scope.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Containment alone grants no control of a child. Not every container is an organizational unit or a valid GPO scope.

Topics.Title: Group Policy objects
Topics.Summary: A GPO has a directory object and policy content in SYSVOL, with separate edit, scope and client-processing conditions.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Review GPO ACLs, link settings, filters, flags and supported computer scope; separately validate SYSVOL and effective policy.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Tessera's GPOAppliesTo model covers supported computer scope only. User/site/loopback policy and actual policy execution are not derived.

Topics.Title: Certificate templates
Topics.Summary: Templates describe certificate purposes, naming, issuance requirements and enrollment permissions.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Use the AD CS review and inspect the exact template's flags, purposes, approval/signatures, publication and enrollment grants.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A matched template configuration alone does not establish ESC1 or certificate issuance.

Topics.Title: Enterprise certificate authorities
Topics.Summary: An enterprise CA publishes templates and may issue certificates. Its directory object and CA service have different permission sources.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Check CAServicePermissionsCollected, imported service ACE summaries, HostingComputer, publication, certificate chain and target-domain trust.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Native directory ACL inventory does not prove CA service enrollment or management. Supported ESC1 derivation currently requires imported direct-root evidence.

Topics.Title: Root CA trust objects
Topics.Summary: RootCA records describe configured directory trust anchors associated with a domain.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Check the captured DomainSid, certificate thumbprint and chain, and match them to the exact CA and target domain.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A thumbprint match models collected trust inventory; it does not validate a live certificate, expiry, revocation or cryptographic signatures.

Topics.Title: Intermediate/AIA certificate authorities
Topics.Summary: AIA CA records preserve certificate authority inventory used by broader certificate-chain analysis.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Review certificate identity and the complete ordered issuer chain against the target domain's configured trust.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Tessera does not yet derive intermediate-chain ESC paths. Presence in AIA alone does not establish domain authentication trust.

Topics.Title: NTAuth certificate stores
Topics.Summary: An NTAuthStore records CA certificate fingerprints designated for domain authentication trust.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Match its captured domain and certificate fingerprints to the exact publishing CA and RootCA evidence.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: NTAuth membership alone is insufficient for ESC1. Enrollment, template, trust-anchor and supported host prerequisites must also hold.

Topics.Title: Certificate issuance policies
Topics.Summary: Issuance-policy OIDs and optional linked groups provide context for certificate issuance and policy review.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Inspect the OID, linked group, template issuance-policy references and actual supported rule prerequisites.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: HasIssuancePolicy and OIDGroupLink are inventory; Tessera does not derive ESC13 group membership from them.

Topics.Title: Domain trust inventory
Topics.Summary: A trust record describes direction, type, attributes and a remote-domain identity.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Interpret direction from the source domain, validate the intended trust relationship, SID filtering and relevant server policy separately.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Tessera retains trust inventory but does not implement general effective trust traversal or every trust-based BloodHound edge.

Topics.Title: AD sites
Topics.Summary: Sites describe directory topology and can influence service/DC selection and policy behavior.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Review related servers and subnets, site configuration and the actual objects in scope.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Site location alone is not a permission, session or endpoint connection. Site GPO applicability is outside the supported scope model.

Topics.Title: Directory site servers
Topics.Summary: A server object links directory site topology to a referenced computer.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Review ServerReferenceDn and the parent site, resolving the actual computer before interpreting endpoint access.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: The server inventory object is distinct from the running computer and from its local authorization.

Topics.Title: Directory site subnets
Topics.Summary: A subnet object associates a network range with an AD site.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Review SiteDn and the configured subnet/site relationship with the directory owner.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A configured subnet association does not prove current host placement, routing or a privilege relationship.

Topics.Title: Referenced or unresolved identities
Topics.Summary: Some SIDs, DNs, SPN hosts or foreign principals appear only as relationship endpoints.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Collect or resolve the referenced object and confirm its stable identity before using names as evidence.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Missing object details reduce confidence and can prevent path resolution. An unresolved reference is not a fabricated user or confirmed control path.

Topics.Title: IDs, names and directory location
Topics.Summary: Id is Tessera's stable graph identifier; Sid/Guid are captured directory identifiers, Dn is a directory location, and names are display/search aids.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Use exact IDs for ambiguous names. A renamed object can keep its SID/GUID while its name or DN changes.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A DN can move and a display name can be duplicated. Do not infer an object's permissions or class from its name.

Topics.Title: Object class and directory type
Topics.Summary: ObjectClasses retains the directory schema classes. Some managed service identities require computer-derived ownership restrictions even when displayed under users.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Check the most specific captured class and derived-type context before interpreting attributes, containment or ownership.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: The viewer's display bucket is not a complete schema classification. Unsupported or conflicting classes suppress some projections.

Topics.Title: Enabled state and UAC
Topics.Summary: Disabled records the captured account state. AccountStateKnown distinguishes a readable account-control value from unavailable information; Uac is the underlying flag mask.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Interpret individual flags and collection time. A null/missing state is unknown and must not be shown as enabled.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Enabled does not prove successful logon, a valid credential, service reachability or absence of authentication restrictions.

Topics.Title: Host, DNS and service names
Topics.Summary: DNS and SPNs help associate services with computer identities; HostingComputer identifies the exact imported CA host. OS is a captured inventory description.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Resolve stable IDs and check aliases, duplicate SPNs and collection time. A CA's host evidence must qualify that same CA.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Ambiguous host aliases are not resolved arbitrarily. A DNS/SPN name is not proof that a service is running or reachable.

Topics.Title: Domain association
Topics.Summary: These identify the object's captured domain or a trust's remote domain; names and SIDs serve different roles.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Match domain SIDs when comparing CA/root/NTAuth or policy evidence. Verify which end of a trust is being described.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Domain membership alone does not establish a usable trust path or cross-domain authorization.

Topics.Title: Security-enabled group state
Topics.Summary: True identifies a captured security group; false identifies a group that does not supply a security token for the relevant model. Missing means unknown.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Read group type from current collection rather than assuming all imported groups are security-enabled.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Several derived GPO, ownership, replication and ESC1 membership rules require a known security-enabled group. Older SharpHound exports may omit this fact.

Sections.Title: Optional import enrichment
Sections.Text: Read missing group types (import) uses the DC and identity from the connection tab. CLI: -ImportSharpHound -EnrichGroupTypes -Server <DC>. Only absent classifications are supplemented, by binary SID with returned objectSid/objectGUID and domain identity checks. Known values are preserved; failed, ambiguous and out-of-domain lookups remain unknown.

Sections.Title: Evidence times
Sections.Text: GroupTypeSource ReadOnlyLDAP identifies a post-export observation, with the DC, returned identity, groupType, read time and change markers retained. Original permissions and memberships are not revalidated. Such data does not make an old export a consistent live snapshot; affected candidates require current validation.

Sections.Title: Original import state
Sections.Text: GroupTypeImportState records Known, Missing or Malformed input classification. SecurityEnabledRaw preserves an invalid source value for inspection; it is not used as a Boolean. Optional LDAP enrichment supplements unknown state without modifying the original export.

Sections.Title: Enrichment result codes
Sections.Text: Resolved means a verified exact-SID reply supplied a supported groupType. KnownInExport preserves an existing imported classification. OutsideSelectedDomain refuses a foreign or non-domain SID. Unavailable means connection/domain verification failed. NotFound, Ambiguous, MissingIdentity, IdentityMismatch, UnreadableGroupType, UnsupportedGroupType and LookupFailed leave state unknown. WorkLimit stops further lookups. uSNChanged and whenChanged are object change markers on the selected DC, not groupType-specific history or proof of replication convergence.

Topics.Title: Delegation flags
Topics.Summary: These flags describe account delegation configuration. Protocol transition and unconstrained delegation are different settings.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Combine flags with exact allowed-service targets or resource-based delegation evidence, account restrictions and current authentication controls.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A flag alone does not establish a currently usable delegation chain or successful impersonation.

Topics.Title: Owner and OWNER RIGHTS context
Topics.Summary: OwnerSid identifies the captured owner. OWNER RIGHTS ACEs, applicable WRITE_DAC grants and relevant denies affect whether ownership is projected as control.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Read the assessment and descriptor-analysis note; distinguish OwnsRaw/WriteOwnerRaw observations from supported or conditional projections.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Missing descriptors, unsupported ACEs or relevant denies can suppress inference. OWNER RIGHTS being present does not mean the owner has unrestricted control.

Topics.Title: Captured ownership policy
Topics.Summary: Captured directory-policy context refines computer/MSA/gMSA ownership behavior: Allow, Block, Restricted, Default or Unknown.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Review the exact mode, target type, same-domain administrator exception evidence and server-enforcement limitations in OWNERSHIP.md.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Default and Unknown are not explicit Allow. Restricted modes need operation-specific evaluation; cross-domain administrator exceptions are not fully modeled.

Topics.Title: GPO link and inheritance settings
Topics.Summary: Link options describe a policy link's enabled/enforced state. GpOptions captures scope inheritance configuration, not a permission grant.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Review the link direction, actual scope class, parent chain, block inheritance and enforced links together.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Enforced does not bypass every policy/security condition. GPLink inventory alone is not a traversable policy-control path.

Topics.Title: GPO settings and collection version
Topics.Summary: These capture policy enablement/version, directory-supported functionality, SYSVOL location and WMI filtering.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Validate supported computer policy flags, no unresolved WMI filtering, and consistency of directory/SYSVOL versions before assessing practical effect.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A SYSVOL path is a location, not proof of file write access. WMI/client processing, policy contents and resultant policy are not evaluated.

Topics.Title: GPO Read/Apply evidence
Topics.Summary: These summaries describe supported Read and Apply permissions from the collected GPO security descriptor.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Inspect the descriptor note and separate membership witnesses for the target computer's Read and Apply prerequisites.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Unknown/unsupported ACLs, relevant denies or conflicting facts suppress modeled applicability. Summary arrays do not establish complete effective-token access.

Topics.Title: Certificate naming and issuance flags
Topics.Summary: Template naming and enrollment masks describe requester-supplied subject and approval behavior; signatures/schema affect issuance requirements. Flags on other object classes have class-specific meanings.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Use the object's actual class. In the template review, subject bit 0x1 differs from SAN-only naming, approval uses bit 0x2, and schema 1 differs from later signature handling.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Do not interpret a generic Flags value as a template flag mask on every class. Missing, malformed or future schema values remain unknown.

Topics.Title: Certificate purposes and policies
Topics.Summary: EKUs/application policies describe intended certificate purposes; issuance-policy OIDs and optional group links are distinct metadata.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Review purpose restrictions, application-policy interactions and issuance requirements together with publication and enrollment rights.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Empty purpose lists may reflect missing/unreadable data and are not automatically unrestricted. An issuance-policy group link does not itself grant membership.

Topics.Title: CA-service permissions and provenance
Topics.Summary: CA-service ACE summaries come from a successful supplied SharpHound CASecurity result. Directory-object ACEs are kept separately.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Check successful collection, failure text, right names, trustees and the exact CA identity. ESC1 requires service Enroll on the same publishing CA.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Directory Enroll/ManageCA observations cannot substitute for actual service evidence. A summarized allow ACE still needs full-token validation.

Topics.Title: Certificate chains and thumbprints
Topics.Summary: Thumbprints identify certificates in the collected inventory; CertChain is ordered, while NTAuth stores list trusted certificate identities.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Match CA, RootCA and NTAuth fingerprints in the same supported target-domain context; inspect the exact CA's host separately.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Current ESC1 derivation supports imported direct-root chains only. A fingerprint is public identity metadata, not a private key or proof of current certificate validity.

Topics.Title: AD CS capture state and denies
Topics.Summary: These retain the source/schema marker, reported deny counts and explicit imported template prerequisites used by supported AD CS rules.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Distinguish a captured false value from an omitted property. Review contradiction/conflict notes and original exported records.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Version/source markers describe the parser's evidence shape; they do not attest that current CA or domain authentication enforcement was tested.

Topics.Title: Published certificate templates
Topics.Summary: The CA directory object lists which templates it publishes. Imported publication is also retained as a template-to-CA observation.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Match the template's stable identity or validated alias to the exact publishing CA.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Publication does not grant enrollment and does not establish that requests will be issued.

Topics.Title: Trust direction, type and attributes
Topics.Summary: These are raw directory trust configuration values and flags describing the recorded trust object.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Interpret direction relative to the source domain and validate the relevant forest/domain policy and SID filtering separately.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Tessera does not translate these fields into complete trust-based privilege traversal. A trust inventory row alone is not an attack path.

Topics.Title: Relationship endpoints and evidence source
Topics.Summary: Source/Target describe the directed relationship; endpoint DN flags indicate identities needing resolution. Derivation names a modeled projection, while EvidenceSource/Authority identify provenance.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Read the relationship type and its source-specific explanation. Match stable endpoints and verify whether the evidence is directory, endpoint, service, imported or derived.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A relationship label can appear in inventory without being traversable. Verified-source flags do not establish full-token effective access or successful execution.

Topics.Title: Captured ACE summaries
Topics.Summary: An ACE summary identifies a trustee, a classified right, reported allow/deny context and inheritance state.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Inspect the original descriptor/source when exact applicability matters. Locate the ancestor where an inherited grant originates rather than editing an unrelated explicit ACE.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: A summary is not a complete effective-access calculation. Inherit-only, object class/property GUIDs, denies and group token conditions can change applicability.

Topics.Title: Conflicting captured evidence
Topics.Summary: A conflict marker records incompatible prerequisite facts across supplied snapshots and survives supported merge round trips.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Return to the original scan folders, compare collection times/scope and collect a consistent current snapshot where needed.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Merging does not justify selecting only the most permissive value. A conflict can suppress a projection without proving that the real capability is denied.

Topics.Title: Membership and scope witnesses
Topics.Summary: A witness records a supporting chain of captured facts used by a derivation, rather than the complete effective token or every possible route.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Follow each chain from the source toward its grant trustee or scope root. DCSync, GPO and ESC1 can require distinct prerequisites reached through different memberships. Confirm that all witnesses refer to the same modeled target and supported rule.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: Witness arrays are bounded previews, generally up to 64 objects. A preview can omit later entries; consult the graph and collection data for the full chain. A witness is not evidence that an operation succeeded or that deny rules were fully evaluated.

Topics.Title: Derived-rule identities and grant provenance
Topics.Summary: These fields identify which exact template, CA, trust objects, scope root or grant trustee supplied the modeled prerequisites.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Match stable IDs to the inspected objects. ESC1 uses the same publishing CA for template and service enrollment, with root and NTAuth trust in the same target domain. GPO LinkRoot and ownership PolicySource describe different rule-specific context.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: One derived edge can retain one representative qualifying composition; Tessera does not expand every alternate CA/template composition. Grant provenance and captured policy are modeling evidence, not live execution or complete effective access.

Topics.Title: Unsupported BloodHound features and unfamiliar labels
Topics.Summary: Help coverage is separate from collection and path-rule support. Tessera does not implement every BloodHound relationship, derivation, platform or query.

Sections.Title: What to check
Sections.Text: Read PATH-PARITY.md and the GPO, ownership and AD CS scope notes for current prerequisites and limits. Check the actual imported bucket, derivation, identity resolution and query filters before expecting a relationship to participate in a route.

Sections.Title: Limits and interpretation
Sections.Text: An imported unfamiliar label may be preserved as inventory without being traversed. Adding help or selecting a glossary entry does not enable that capability. Consult the original BloodHound documentation for features outside the supported model.
